steps.title: Import TestBed, ComponentFixture, and Component from Angular testing utilities
steps.instruction: Import TestBed and ComponentFixture from '@angular/core/testing' and Component from '@angular/core'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import multiple symbols from the same module.
steps.seedCode: // Import TestBed, ComponentFixture, and Component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The testing utilities are imported and ready to be used for component testing.
successCriteria: TestBed and ComponentFixture are imported from '@angular/core/testing', and Component is imported from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the core testing utilities needed for Angular component testing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some of the required utilities. Make sure to import TestBed and ComponentFixture from '@angular/core/testing' and Component from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are not correct. You need to import TestBed and ComponentFixture from '@angular/core/testing' and Component from '@angular/core'.

steps.title: Create a simple test component class
steps.instruction: Define a simple Angular component class named TestComponent with a template that contains a heading element displaying 'Test Component'.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator to define the component's selector and template. The template should be a simple string containing an <h1> element.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a TestComponent class that can be used in your TestBed configuration for testing.
successCriteria:
TestComponent class is defined with @Component decorator, selector 'app-test', and template '

Test Component

'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a simple test component class. This component will serve as the subject for our testing demonstrations.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your component has the @Component decorator with both selector and template properties defined correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component definition seems incomplete or incorrect. Check that you've used the @Component decorator with the required properties.

steps.title: Configure the testing module with TestBed
steps.instruction: Inside a describe block (or before your test), call TestBed.configureTestingModule() and pass an object with a declarations array containing your TestComponent.
steps.hint: Use TestBed.configureTestingModule({ declarations: [TestComponent] }) to set up the testing module.
steps.expectedOutcome: The testing module is configured with TestComponent declared, ready for creating the component fixture.
successCriteria: TestBed.configureTestingModule is called with an object containing declarations: [TestComponent].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully configured the testing module with TestBed.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling TestBed.configureTestingModule() and passing the correct configuration object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The testing module isn't configured correctly. Use TestBed.configureTestingModule() with declarations: [TestComponent].

steps.title: Compile the testing module
steps.instruction: Call TestBed.compileComponents() to compile the testing module after the TestBed configuration.
steps.hint: Add TestBed.compileComponents() after the TestBed.configureTestingModule call. This is an async operation that prepares components for testing.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: compiling a testing module
TestBed.compileComponents();
steps.expectedOutcome: The testing module will be compiled, allowing components to be instantiated in tests.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully compiled the testing module. This step ensures components are ready for instantiation.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you call TestBed.compileComponents() after the TestBed configuration.
steps.feedbackWrong: The testing module compilation step is missing. Add TestBed.compileComponents() after the TestBed.configureTestingModule call.

steps.title: Create the component fixture
steps.instruction: Call TestBed.createComponent() to create a ComponentFixture for the TestComponent and assign it to a variable named fixture.
steps.hint: Use TestBed.createComponent(TestComponent) to create the fixture. Store the result in a const variable with type ComponentFixture<TestComponent>.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a fixture for a component
const fixture: ComponentFixture<TestComponent> = TestBed.createComponent(TestComponent);
steps.expectedOutcome: A fixture variable is created that holds the ComponentFixture instance for TestComponent.
successCriteria: TestBed.createComponent(TestComponent) is called and the result is assigned to a variable named fixture with type ComponentFixture<TestComponent>.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the component fixture. The fixture gives you access to the component instance and its DOM element for testing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling TestBed.createComponent(TestComponent) and storing the result in a variable named fixture.
steps.feedbackWrong: The fixture wasn't created correctly. You need to call TestBed.createComponent(TestComponent) and assign it to a variable.

steps.title: Access the component instance
steps.instruction: Access the component instance from the fixture and store it in a variable named 'componentInstance'.
steps.hint: Use fixture.componentInstance to get the component instance.
steps.analogousExample:
// Accessing a component instance
const componentInstance = fixture.componentInstance;
steps.expectedOutcome: The component instance is retrieved and stored in a variable for later use in tests.
successCriteria: The component instance is accessed using fixture.componentInstance and stored in a variable named 'componentInstance'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully accessed the component instance from the fixture.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using fixture.componentInstance and storing it in a variable named 'componentInstance'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to access the component instance using fixture.componentInstance and store it in a variable.

steps.title: Trigger change detection
steps.instruction: Call fixture.detectChanges() to trigger initial change detection after creating the component fixture.
steps.hint: Use the fixture variable you created earlier and call its detectChanges() method.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component's template will be rendered and any initial data bindings will be processed.
successCriteria: fixture.detectChanges() is called after creating the component fixture.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've triggered change detection, which ensures the component's template is rendered and initial data bindings are processed.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling detectChanges() on the fixture variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try calling fixture.detectChanges() to trigger the initial change detection cycle.

steps.title: Access the native DOM element
steps.instruction: Access the native DOM element from the fixture and store it in a variable called 'nativeElement'.
steps.hint: Use fixture.nativeElement to get the rendered DOM element.
steps.analogousExample:
// Accessing a DOM element in a test
let element = fixture.nativeElement;
steps.expectedOutcome: The native DOM element is accessible via fixture.nativeElement and stored in a variable.
successCriteria: A variable named 'nativeElement' is declared and assigned the value of fixture.nativeElement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully accessed the native DOM element, which allows you to inspect the rendered HTML.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using fixture.nativeElement and storing it in a variable called 'nativeElement'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't match what we need. Use fixture.nativeElement to get the DOM element and store it in a variable named 'nativeElement'.

steps.title: Write a test to verify component creation
steps.instruction: Write an expect statement to verify the component instance exists. Use the component variable you already declared.
steps.hint: Use the expect function with component as the argument and chain .toBeTruthy() to assert it exists.
steps.expectedOutcome: A test assertion is added to verify the component instance exists.
successCriteria: An expect statement checks that component is truthy using .toBeTruthy().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've written a basic test assertion to verify the component was created successfully.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the component variable and calling .toBeTruthy() on it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test assertion is missing or incorrect. Use expect(component).toBeTruthy() to verify the component instance exists.

steps.title: Write a test to verify template content
steps.instruction: Write an expect statement to check if the paragraph text 'Test Component' appears in the native DOM element.
steps.hint: Use the nativeElement's textContent property and the toContain matcher to verify the expected text.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: verifying text content in a test
expect(nativeElement.textContent).toContain('Expected Text');
steps.expectedOutcome: The test now verifies that the component's template renders the expected text content.
successCriteria: An expect statement is added that checks if nativeElement.textContent contains 'Test Component'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully written a test to verify the template content. This ensures your component renders the expected UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using nativeElement.textContent and the toContain matcher to check for 'Test Component'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test for template content isn't quite right. You need to write an expect statement that checks if the paragraph text appears in the DOM.
